title: DICTONIC Bonds: from the Octet to the Rule of Halves
description:
DICTO proposed that his bond papers are one series building to the Rule of Halves. A DICTONIC bond is a pair of pieces that fill space together: the Golden bond (Icosaxes and Unborn Axes), the Keyed bond (Lotus Jewel Axes and Dodecaxes), the Delian bond (Samson and Delilah) and the Twinned Delian bond (Sonsam and Lahdeli). This book follows the series from filling space with mixed solids, through the bonds and the web of shared faces between neighbouring pieces, to the Rule of Halves for every close-packed stacking.

Eleven chapters, each a published paper with its theorems and proofs word for word, in five parts. Part I, Filling: (1) Every Mix of the Platonic Solids Fills Space (#47): all 31 mixes of the Platonic solids fill space at one edge length with a kit of seven connectors. (2) One Move Each (#50): five classical cut-and-glue space-fillers, each obtained exactly by one setting of three moves, a shear, the equal-edged cell and a stretch. Part II, The bonds: (3) The Golden Split (#48): cutting every AXE at the golden point 1/φ turns the icosahedra and the Unborns into two convex space-fillers, the Icosaxes and the Unborn Axes, and no other cut point does. (4) The Delian Bond (#51): one flat cut slid through the octet runs from Kepler's rhombic dodecahedron to the cube, with Samson and Delilah of equal volume at one point. Part III, The web: (5) The Web of Bonds (#52): the golden and Delian loops are power diagrams of one fixed set of points with one weight slid between two kinds; the unlike bond never breaks, the like bonds hand over. (6) The Global Web of Bonds (#53): the same two hand-overs in ten further crystal networks. Part IV, The weight walk's bonds: (7) David and Goliath (#55): in A15, one exact weight gives Goliath, the hull of Jessen's orthogonal icosahedron, with David. (8) Sonsam and Lahdeli (#56): the equal-volume pair of the twinned octet, with Ian Dury, Blockhead and keyed switch points. (9) The Icosaxes Hexa (#59): twenty Icosaxes close into one solid, the Icosaxes Seed. Part V, The law: (10) From the Octet to Every Stacking (#58): the series told as one route. (11) The Rule of Halves (#57): in every close-packed stacking each piece is borrowed, whole or in half, from the cubic or the hexagonal stacking, so the pieces are finite in kind.

With a preface, an epilogue, the sources of every chapter gathered in one appendix, and an index. Nothing new is proved in the book; it puts the published papers in one order as one series. __PAGES__ pages. The cover is the DICTONIC square. The ideas and names are DICTO's. Computation and proof with Claude (Anthropic). Licence CC BY-SA 4.0. More at dictospheres.com.
